details.full_text:
The X is for eXtremes: @JAXA_en's XRISM X-ray space telescope is set to launch to explore the largest structures, hottest regions, and objects with the strongest gravity in the universe.

Follow @XRISM_jp and @NASAUniverse for updates, and watch liftoff here: https://t.co/cT5YDFFsHa

media_entities2.ext_alt_text: A completed X-ray Mirror Assembly for the X-ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission. The assembly has thin metal struts fanning outward from a silver ring in the center of the image. Shiny ridge surfaces (actually many thin mirrors!) fill in the spaces between the struts. The image is watermarked with the text “Credit: Taylor Mickal/NASA.”

profile_bio.description: Your backstage pass to the universe and how NASA studies it. Exoplanets, black holes, dark energy, and more!

details.full_text:
Let’s do launch!

In a few hours, @JAXA_en will be launching a new eye on the X-ray sky. We’re counting down to XRISM’s trip to space tonight, Aug. 27, at 8:26 p.m. ET (Aug. 28, 9:26 a.m. Japan).

What do you hope XRISM will help us learn about the cosmos? https://t.co/IKsOK19Wtw

media_entities2.ext_alt_text: This photograph shows the upper rocket section being fitted with the H-IIA payload fairing containing JAXA’s XRISM telescope in the days leading up to launch. A tall white cylinder fills the center of the image, featuring small dots of fasteners and several metallic attachments. It is being connected by several technicians in light-colored protective clothing and hard hats to a round yellow surface that extends into the floor below. A large segmented yellow hose sticks out of the left side of the fairing and extends upward, out of the image. A white wall with stairs and lighting is in the background, and smaller silver rolling stairs are around the work site, which also has various tools and safety signs. The image is watermarked with “(c)JAXA.”
